Calculate radial profiles

Source: R/calculate_profiles.R
calculate_sector_profiles.Rd

calculate_sector_profiles() divides the cells of each ring into n_sectors equal-width sectors (by relative radial position) and computes per-sector means and optionally quantiles of the selected cell parameters. The returned QWAprofile object includes a column sector_n with values in [1,..., n_sectors] for each image_label and year.

calculate_band_profiles() computes moving-band profiles of selected cell parameters across the ring width. Each band is a window of bandwidth microns that shifts in steps of stepsize microns from the innner to the outer ring boundary. The returned QWAprofile object includes columns start and end with the band limits in microns (with the mrw value for context) for each image_label and year.

For each selected parameter, the returned columns include number of valid cells used in the aggregation (<param>_N), the mean (<param>_mean) for each sector or band, and the quantile columns for the given probabilities (named by percentage, e.g. la_q25, la_q05, la_q25.7).

Usage

calculate_sector_profiles(
  QWA_data,
  n_sectors,
  sel_cell_params,
  quant_probs = NULL,
  apply_exclusions = FALSE,
  tissue = c("all", "affected")
)

calculate_band_profiles(
  QWA_data,
  bandwidth,
  stepsize,
  sel_cell_params,
  quant_probs = NULL,
  band_rebound = TRUE,
  apply_exclusions = FALSE,
  tissue = c("all", "affected")
)

Arguments

QWA_data

A QWAdata object with a non-NULL $cells component (and $rings component for calculate_band_profiles()).

n_sectors

Number of equal-width sectors to divide each ring into.

sel_cell_params

Character vector of cell parameters to include in the profiles (either a subset of the measurement column names of QWA_data$cells, e.g. c("la", "cwtrad"), or "all"). NOTE: using "all" results in a large number of columns in the returned QWAprofile.

quant_probs

Numeric vector of distinct quantile probabilities in [0, 1] (e.g. c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)). Set NULL or empty to derive only means.

apply_exclusions

If TRUE, the cells of excluded rings (exclude_dupl, exclude_issues in $rings) are filtered out, returning 'clean' measurement series ready for analyses. Default FALSE.

tissue

Only used with apply_exclusions = TRUE. "all" (default) removes all cells of excluded rings; "affected" removes only the earlywood or latewood cells (by ew_lw) of rings with exclude_issues and affected_tissue "ew" or "lw", respectively.

bandwidth

Width of each band in microns.

stepsize

Step size between band starts in microns.

band_rebound

If TRUE (default), the last band is shifted so its end coincides exactly with the ring width (mrw).

Value

A QWAprofile object with profile_type = "sector" or profile_type = "band".

Details

In order to use apply_exclusions = TRUE, the QWA_data$rings component must be provided and include the flag columns exclude_dupl and exclude_issues. In addition, to exclude only the cells from affected tissue (via tissue = "affected"), the ew_lw assignment in $cells must exist (see complete_QWAdata()). The exclusion flag and affected_tissue columns can be edited via launch_flags_app() before the profile calculation, if you want a 'clean' profile object that does not include rows from overlapping or problematic rings (or tissue).

To return a ew_band column in a band-type QWAprofile (indicating if a band falls entirely within the earlywood), the $rings component must include an eww column, which can be added via complete_QWAdata().
